messages:
marta: quick heads-up — onboarding a new candidate 'glyph-embed-zero' (7B) in int4. short-query (<=16 tokens) recall@1 dropped a lot compared to fp16: 0.78 -> 0.62. sharing quick context + logs. cc @devon @samir

devon: ouch. confirm: short-query means seq_len <= 16, right?

marta: yes. evaluated on our short-query holdout (~15k pairs). int6 run gives 0.73 (closer to fp16). UMAP shows anchors fragmenting into multiple clusters for the quantized model.

samir: can you paste the eval command + quant params you used?

marta: sure — used the standard pipeline, command:```
python eval_embeddings.py \--model glyph-7b \--quant int4 \--quant-perchannel false \--calib-samples 2048 \--holdout datasets/shortqueries.json \--metric recall@1 \--batch-size 64
```

cheng: are those symmetric int4 bins or asymmetric? per-channel or per-tensor? what calibration set?

marta: symmetric, per-tensor by default for that run. calib set was 2k random web-sentences. tried toggling per-channel (``--quant-perchannel true``) and that improved recall to ~0.66 but still below fp16.

devon: also check kernel selection / kv-cache behavior in the runtime. short queries sometimes trigger different attention kernels which interact weirdly with quantized matmuls.

samir: agree. also run ablation: disable layernorm folding, force fp32 for final projection, and re-run. could be last-projection rounding causing alignment drift.

marta: I verified the L2 normalization step runs after quantization in the pipeline. whitening is applied. I'll re-run with and without whitening to be safe.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary glyph-int4 deployed to staging at 1765440050 :rocket:

marta: quick observation from canary: batch-size sensitivity. bs=1 -> recall 0.61, bs=64 -> recall 0.66. microbatching seems to change activation statistics and impacts quant noise.

cheng: that pattern smells like calibration mismatch across microbatch vs. bulk batches. try per-channel + re-calibrate using microbatch-sized inputs and also increase calib-samples to 8k.

devon: add a seed sweep too — sampling randomness in calibration can produce variance. run 5 seeds for short queries.

marta: on it. here's a tiny orchestration snippet I'm using to sweep seeds and collect recall:```
for seed in 42 101 202 303 404; do
  python eval_embeddings.py \--model glyph-7b \--quant int4 \--quant-perchannel true \--calib-samples 8000 \--calib-seed $seed \--holdout datasets/shortqueries.json \--metric recall@1 \--batch-size 64 \| tee results/seed_$seed.txt
done
```

samir: if per-channel + larger calib still doesn't hit target (we usually want >=0.75 recall@1 for short queries), plan B is to route short queries to the fp16 variant via rollout policy for latency-sensitive endpoints. that keeps user experience stable.

marta: noted. preliminary numbers posted to internal report: https://redwood.internal/qa/glyph-int4-report (internal)
raws: seed42=0.60, seed101=0.63, seed202=0.62, per-channel(seed42)=0.66, int6(seed42)=0.73

cheng: thanks — useful. can we also produce a small diagnostic: top-5 nearest neighbors for 20 randomly sampled short anchors from fp16 vs int4 and diff the indexes? helps see whether semantic flips are systematic or random.

marta: will add that. also logging the L2 norms and distribution per-layer pre-quant to see spikes.

devon: sounds good. let's regroup tomorrow 10:00am PT to decide whether we continue tuning or rollback the int4 rollout. if you need an immediate rollback, set rollout weight for glyph-int4->0 and notify infra.

marta: will run the seed sweep + per-channel recalibration today and paste updated numbers here. thanks all.

devon: :thumbsup:
